about.heroTitle: Connecting Nepali student talent with the work that matters
about.heroSubtitle: Aavasar is a marketplace where students earn real money and real experience while businesses across Nepal hire vetted, motivated talent — quickly, transparently, and at a fair price.
about.story1: Aavasar started with a simple frustration: Nepal is full of skilled, ambitious students — and businesses that desperately need their skills — but the two sides almost never meet at the right time.
about.story2: Students were stuck choosing between unpaid internships and gigs that didn't fit their schedule. Recruiters were posting to noisy job boards and waiting weeks for a single qualified applicant. We built Aavasar to close that gap.
about.story3: Today, students join free, build a verified portfolio, and apply to paid gigs that match their skills. Recruiters post a role, screen applicants the same day, and message the right person directly — no middlemen, no surprises.
about.missionLead: Make professional work-experience accessible to every Nepali student, and make hiring vetted talent a same-week decision for every Nepali business.
about.mission1: Students earn while they study and graduate with a real portfolio.
about.mission2: Recruiters hire vetted talent in days, not months — at a fair price.
about.mission3: Every transaction is transparent, in NPR, and protected.
about.pillarsSubtitle: We're not a generic job board. Every feature is designed for the way Nepali students and recruiters actually work.
about.pillar1Body: Aavasar is designed around how students in Nepal actually work — flexible hours, gigs that fit a class schedule, and pay in NPR with no foreign-exchange friction.
about.pillar2Body: Every student profile is reviewed before it goes live, and recruiters verify their company before posting. Trust is the product.
about.pillar3Body: Recruiters post a gig, see qualified applicants the same day, and message candidates directly. No agencies, no inflated fees.
about.teamSubtitle: A small founding team based in Kathmandu, building Aavasar from the ground up.
